overall: The AG found two emails sent by the Committee co-chair to a quorum constituted unlawful deliberation, an individual violation but not a Committee violation; no serial quorum deliberation or other violations were found.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a series of email communications among a quorum of the building committee, facilitated by co-chairs, discussed and shaped views on a citizens' petition article.
allegations.key_passage: Ms. Sturgis' April 30, 2011 email to 10 of the 11 members of the Committee, attaching a presentation and requesting comments, constituted an unlawful deliberation outside of a posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Co-chair's May 7, 2011 email to all members soliciting opinions on a public records request was alleged to be deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, Ms. Sturgis' May 7, 2011 email to the 11 other members of the Committee, soliciting opinions or information regarding a public records request submitted to the Committee, also constituted improper deliberation, as it was sent to a quorum of the Committee and regarded public business within its jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a serial deliberation by a quorum through a chain of emails; the AG found no quorum serial deliberation occurred.
allegations.key_passage: With regard to the remaining 28 emails that we reviewed, none were between or among a quorum of the Committee. We therefore find no violation of the Open Meeting Law with respect to these messages, nor do we find that a quorum of the Committee engaged in a serial deliberation as alleged by the complainant.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee as a whole violated the law by deliberating through member emails on strategy to defeat a citizens' petition article and ballot question.
allegations.key_passage: However, we do not find a violation by the Committee as a whole because there is no evidence that any Committee member responded to a quorum of the Committee.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Publicly disclose the two emails discussed in the letter at the Committee's next meeting.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law. Additionally, we order the Committee to publicly disclose the two emails discussed in this letter at its next meeting.
